thread:
maria: FYI — after the RBAC tweak that tightened service-account-to-keystore binding in eu-west, we started seeing a spike of TLS handshake failures on the internal ingress-to-service path (ingress-proxy -> annotation-service) around 06:12 UTC. 502s and 'remote error: tls: bad certificate' in the proxy logs.

teo: seen it. grabbing logs now, seems scoped to eu-west nodes only. any KMS decrypt denies?

maria: yes, KMS audit shows a bunch of Deny on kms:Decrypt for role arn:aws:iam::111111:role/ingress-proxy-eu. sample: 
```
2024-06-05T06:12:18Z ingress-proxy eu-west-1: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: user role ingress-proxy-eu not in keystore-decrypt-binding
```

riley: that matches — RBAC change removed the old keystore binding while we rolled out the new sigchain. We pinned cert identity to old SA in the proxy (ingress.identity=v1). When KMS denies decrypt, the proxy can't unwrap ephemeral client cert, so ingress presents expired client cert to backend -> handshake fail.

sanjay: quick Q: can ingress fallback to cached cert or a less strict validation while we roll back? Need minimal blast radius.

maria: we have two mitigations: 1) hot rollback of the RBAC change (fast, but reopens the previous weaker binding) 2) temporary allowlist in keystore policy for ingress-proxy-eu role (scoped, short TTL) + force a coordinated cert refresh. Prefer #2 if we can push policy change quickly.

teo: agree prefer scoped policy change. I'll open a policy-change PR and tag infra-oncall. Estimated deploy < 15m once approved. Need confirmation of exact role ARNs.

riley: ARNs: ingress-proxy-eu, ingress-proxy-eu-canary, annotation-service-eu. Also we should add an audit filter so any KMS.Decrypt Deny with those roles alerts on call channel.

maria: deploy-bot: can we do a controlled policy change to add a one-line allowlist for kms:Decrypt for role ingress-proxy-eu with condition RestrictTo: 2024-06-05T07:00:00Z?

deploy-bot: @maria — created PR https://git.internal/rbac/policies/1234, CI checks passed, awaiting codeowner approval.

sanjay: also, block scope: add a tenant label so this can't be abused cross-region. Put a 30m TTL and add an immediate audit entry. We should not leave it open.

teo: doing the TTL via policy condition now, will include aws:RequestTag/ephemeral=true and aws:RequestTime <= 2024-06-05T07:00:00Z. Pushing changes to PR.

maria: ops-bot — please create an incident ticket and link to PR; severity P2 for now.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-342 created: "eu-west ingress-to-service TLS failures after keystore RBAC tighten". Pager oncall: @sanjay.

riley: post-mitigation checklist: 1) verify handshake success across 10 test paths in eu-west 2) rotate ephemeral certs on ingress 3) run the cert-validator smoke suite 4) run KMS audit queries for Deny -> resolved.

maria: I'll run smoke after PR is merged. If green, we'll do canary rollout (5% nodes) then full. If anything else pops, revert PR and proceed with full RBAC rollback.

teo: timeline: PR approval + apply ~8m, cert refresh ~4m, canary 10m. total ~22m. tagging legal/compliance for the temporary exception.

sanjay: after we stabilize, we need a follow-up CR to: remove allowlist, update proxy identity pinning to accept new-role signatures, and add automated test gating on RBAC changes so this doesn't regress.

maria: agreed. I'll own the follow-up and draft runbook snippets. leaving notes for postmortem: include KMS audit sample lines, proxy cert unwrap path, RBAC change diff, and suggestion to require canary RBAC rollout in staging eu-west before prod.

teo: one more action: add a transient alert rule: if KMS.Decrypt Deny rate for any ingress proxy role > 5/min for 5m -> page sec-oncall. riley can you add?

riley: adding now. alert rule created and tested.

maria: PR merged and applied. starting cert refresh on 10 canary nodes.

teo: canary is green, handoff to riley to kick off full rollout when ready.

riley: kicking full rollout. monitoring TLs.

maria: all clear after rollout, handshake errors back to baseline. closing incident after 1h stability window. I'll open the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
